compiled_state.title: As a reconciler operator, I want the 5 unimplemented inbound applier leaves to write real local-ticket changes when dispatched, and a structural test guaranteeing _LEAVES never again points at a no-op body
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## What
Implement the 5 unimplemented `_apply_inbound_*` leaves (`create`, `update`, `delete`, `repair_property` wire-up, `conflict`) so each performs its documented behavior. Add a structural `_LEAVES` registry coverage test that prevents future no-op stubs from passing CI.

## Why
6 of 7 inbound leaves in `applier.py` are empty stubs that return `ApplyResult(direction, action, {})` without performing any work. This is the central bug behind epic 4047 closing P1=PASS with the load-bearing implementation unbuilt (bug 1761).

## Done Definitions
- `applier.apply([Mutation(direction=inbound, action=create, target='DIG-123', payload={'fields': {'summary': 'X', 'priority': 2, 'status': 'To Do', 'issuetype': 'Task'}, 'comments': [], 'labels': []})], pass_id, repo_root)` against a fixture repo produces `.tickets-tracker/jira-dig-123/001-CREATE.json` AND `ticket show jira-dig-123` outputs summary='X', priority=2, status='To Do', type='task', tags include 'imported:reconciler-bootstrap'. Dispatch path pinned: `_LEAVES[(inbound, create)]` resolves to the function under test. ← Satisfies: sc-1, sc-6
- `applier.apply([Mutation(direction=inbound, action=update, target='jira-dig-123', payload={'fields': {'summary': 'Y'}})], pass_id, repo_root)` against a fixture where jira-dig-123 already exists produces a new event file in the same ticket directory AND `ticket show jira-dig-123` reflects summary='Y'. Dispatch path: `_LEAVES[(inbound, update)]`. ← Satisfies: sc-1, sc-6
- `applier.apply([Mutation(direction=inbound, action=delete, target='jira-dig-123', payload={'probe_outcome': 'hard_delete'})], pass_id, repo_root)` against a fixture produces an event indicating the documented hard-delete disposition (preserve local content + emit follow-on `(outbound, create_after_hard_delete)`). Same shape covers the other 3 probe branches (redirect, out_of_window, trash) via parametrized test. Dispatch path: `_LEAVES[(inbound, delete)]`. ← Satisfies: sc-1, sc-6
- `_LEAVES[(inbound, repair_property)]` resolves to the function whose body invokes `client.set_issue_property` (currently at applier.py:1110 — dead code). Smoke test: `_apply_typed(Mutation(direction=inbound, action=repair_property, target='DIG-X', payload={'local_id': 'L'}))` with a mock client → `client.set_issue_property` called once with arguments ('DIG-X', 'dso_local_id', 'L'). The stub at applier.py:318 is removed. ← Satisfies: sc-1, sc-6
- `_apply_inbound_conflict` files a bug ticket via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket create bug` AND emits a follow-on `{'kind': 'suppress_pair', 'local_id': ..., 'jira_key': ...}` signal that `reconcile_once` honors by removing all subsequent mutations targeting the same pair from the manifest. Test: fixture with 1 conflict + 2 follow-on update mutations on the same pair → manifest contains the conflict bug filing + zero updates for that pair. Dispatch path: `_LEAVES[(inbound, conflict)]`. ← Satisfies: sc-1, sc-6
- Structural registry assertion: new test file `tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_leaves_registry_coverage.py` iterates every `_LEAVES` entry; for each, asserts the function source (`inspect.getsource`) has ≥10 effective code lines (non-blank, non-comment) OR contains a regex match for `client\\.|ticket\\.|\\.write_text|\\.append|subprocess\\.run`. Test FAILS today (5 stubs); MUST PASS at story closure. ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Unit tests pass (exit 0); lint passes; format check passes. ← Validates Closure Check: "TDD DoD"

## Implementation Notes
- Local ticket creation uses `.claude/scripts/dso ticket create <type> "<title>" -d "..." --tags imported:reconciler-bootstrap`; the shim invokes the orphan-branch ticket CLI.
- Issue-type mapping: Jira `Bug` → local `bug`; `Story` → `story`; `Task` → `task`; `Epic` → `epic`; default (any other) → `task`. Encoded as a dict in `mutation.py` or a new `inbound_mapping.py`.
- Status mapping reverse direction: derived from existing `local_to_jira_status` config by inverting; if ambiguous (multiple local statuses map to same Jira status), pick first lexicographic and document.
- Hard-delete branch: emit `(outbound, create_after_hard_delete)` follow-on; reconcile_once handles in same pass. If too complex, the delete leaf may defer the follow-on with a documented limitation comment; in that case file a follow-on task (NOT story).
- `_apply_inbound_repair_property` wire-up: rename the function at line 1110 to `_apply_inbound_repair_property` and remove the stub at line 318 (cleanest path). Verify all existing tests of the line-1110 function still pass under the new name.

## Closure Checks
- All 6 leaves invoked via `_LEAVES` dispatch path observably mutate state per their DD.
- `test_leaves_registry_coverage.py` passes in CI.
- No new "deferred to operator" DDs.
